title: Planner: Capacity view shows who is working on what
summary: Hold: the cost section says every user who needs Capacity view needs a Plan 3 licence, although the same section correctly reports that Plan 5 includes all Plan 3 capabilities. This could lead to unnecessary licence purchases for existing Plan 5 users. The rollout, default state and documented controls otherwise match the supplied notice and Microsoft documentation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cited service description and notice do not give the Plan 3 subscription price.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Capacity view pricing meter credit rate separate charge Plan 3. Read the complete Planner service description and supplied MC1474110; neither gives a Plan 3 price (the description links to a separate pricing page).

claims.claim: The cited pages publish no meter, credit rate or separate charge specifically for Capacity view.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Capacity view pricing meter credit rate separate charge Plan 3. Read Planner service description, planner-for-admins, manage-planner-app, disable-planner, Update-M365TeamsApp and MC1474110; no Capacity view-specific meter, rate or separate charge appears.

claims.claim: The cost is the Plan 3 licence for any user who needs the view.
claims.quote: The service description also says Planner and Project Plan 5 includes all Planner and Project Plan 3 capabilities ... The cost is therefore the Plan 3 licence for any user who needs the view
claims.fix: Replace 'The cost is therefore the Plan 3 licence for any user who needs the view' with 'For users not already entitled through Planner and Project Plan 3 or an existing Planner and Project Plan 5 subscription, access can require purchasing Planner and Project Plan 3'. Keep the following admin-time clause. The cited service description states that Plan 5 includes all Plan 3 capabilities.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block turns off the Planner app at organisation level.
claims.quote: In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> changes the app's tenant blocked state.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module ... -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. ... -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. ... Type: Boolean

claims.claim: No admin UI equivalent of the organisation-wide IsPlannerAllowed control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner turn off organization admin UI IsPlannerAllowed Set-PlannerConfiguration; "IsPlannerAllowed" admin center UI Planner organization. Read disable-planner, planner-for-admins, manage-planner-app and FAQ excerpts; only PowerShell sets IsPlannerAllowed, not the Teams app UI.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false is documented for turning off Planner for the organisation.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell. ... Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false

claims.claim: A global admin runs the Planner organisation-level PowerShell control.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell.

claims.quote: Searched: "Capacity view" Planner admin switch disable PowerShell Graph beta configuration. Read manage-planner-app and disable-planner in full; neither mentions Capacity view or a view-specific switch. Their documented operations disable the app or Planner within the stated scope.
